title: Selling and Promotion - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Selling: Nature and Process
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following best defines the primary goal of the selling function in marketing?
options: To create visually appealing advertisements for a wide audience.
To respond to customer needs and wants through planned, personalized communication to influence purchase decisions.
To determine the most efficient distribution channels for a product.
To establish the overarching legal guidelines for a corporation.
questions.explain: Selling is fundamentally about personalized communication aimed at influencing a customer's purchase decision while satisfying their needs and wants.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: In the selling process, what is the 'pre-approach' phase?
options: Greeting the customer face-to-face for the first time.
Asking the customer questions to determine their exact needs.
Gathering information about a prospective client or product before the actual sales meeting.
Following up with the customer after a purchase has been made.
questions.explain: The pre-approach involves all the preparation a salesperson does before physically contacting the customer, such as researching the prospect and reviewing product knowledge.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the term for potential customers who have shown an interest in a product or service but have not yet made a purchase?
options: Suspects
Promoters
Leads or Prospects
Advocates
questions.explain: Leads or prospects are individuals or businesses that might need the product and have the ability to pay for it, making them the target of the sales approach.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: During a sales presentation, a customer states, 'This software seems too complicated for my team to learn.' This statement is an example of a(n):
options: Close
Objection
Feature
Buying signal
questions.explain: An objection is an honest reason, hesitation, or doubt a customer has about making a purchase. Addressing objections is a critical step in the selling process.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which technique is a salesperson using when they ask a customer, 'Would you prefer the delivery on Tuesday or Thursday?' to finalize a sale?
options: Direct close
Trial close
Choice close (or Alternative close)
Service close
questions.explain: An alternative or choice close asks the customer to choose between two or more options, assuming they have already decided to buy.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Why is the 'determining needs' step so vital to a successful sales presentation?
options: It allows the salesperson to recommend the right product by understanding the customer's specific problems or desires.
It tricks the customer into admitting they need a more expensive item.
It is required by federal trade laws before quoting a price.
It gives the salesperson time to process the customer's payment.
questions.explain: Determining needs ensures the salesperson pitches a product that genuinely solves the customer's problem, making the presentation relevant and effective.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

options: Suggesting that a customer should buy a competitor's product.
Recommending additional, related, or complementary products that enhance the original purchase.
Closing the sale before the customer has explicitly said yes.
Suggesting that the customer return at a later date for a discount.
questions.explain: Suggestion selling involves recommending additional items (like a protective case for a new phone) that will save the customer time or money and enhance their experience.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'cold calling' in the selling process?
options: Contacting customers who have already bought from you.
Calling a prospect who has no prior expectation of being contacted by the salesperson.
Meeting clients in a cold-weather climate.
Calling a customer immediately after they abandoned an online shopping cart.
questions.explain: Cold calling is the act of approaching a potential customer without any prior interaction or expressed interest on their part.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: In B2B (Business-to-Business) selling, the purchase decisions are typically:
options: Based entirely on emotional motives.
Made quickly at the cash register without much research.
More complex, involving multiple decision-makers and higher financial stakes.
Done strictly through social media influencers.
questions.explain: B2B sales involve higher price points, formal budgets, and multiple stakeholders, leading to a longer and more analytical buying process compared to B2C.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a salesperson 'qualifying' a prospect?
options: To ensure the prospect is legally old enough to sign a contract.
To determine if the prospect has the need, authority, and financial ability to buy.
To assign a specific tax code to their customer profile.
To practice the sales pitch before meeting real customers.
questions.explain: Qualifying means evaluating a lead to see if they are worth spending sales time on, usually based on BANT criteria: Budget, Authority, Need, and Timeline.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: If a customer states, 'Your price is much higher than I expected,' what kind of objection is this?
options: Product objection
Time objection
Price/Value objection
Source objection
questions.explain: Price objections occur when the customer feels the cost outweighs the perceived value of the product.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: The 'boomerang method' is used by salespeople to:
options: Ensure the customer returns to the store next week.
Turn a customer's objection into the exact reason they should buy the product.
Throw the product to the customer to show its durability.
Offer a refund if the customer does not like the item.
questions.explain: The boomerang method uses the customer's objection as a selling point. E.g., if a jacket is too lightweight, the salesperson points out that makes it perfect for travel.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: During a B2B sales pitch, the salesperson asks, 'How is the current inefficiency in your software costing your business financially?' What step in the selling process is this?
options: Prospecting
Closing
Determining needs
Overcoming objections
questions.explain: Asking probing, open-ended questions about a company's problems is part of determining needs, often utilizing consultative sales methods.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
